Chapter 9: Critique as Care—The Importance of Speaking Up
You know, it’s easy to think that criticism is all about negativity—that if you point out a problem, you’re just complaining.
But real critique? It’s actually an act of care. It’s a way of saying, “I believe this could be so much better.”
When someone refuses to accept easy answers, or asks tough questions, they’re not just tearing things down. They’re making room for something new to grow.
Picture this: a group of coworkers settles in to watch a new show together. Most of them are loving it, laughing along—except for one person. She hesitates, then points out a scene that just didn’t sit right, or a joke that missed the mark.
The others? Well, they might roll their eyes, maybe call her too sensitive. But she stands her ground. She explains why it matters, how even small things can add up, and how the stories we tell shape the way we see the world.
Speaking up like that isn’t easy. It can mean being labeled as difficult, or negative, or even a killjoy. But here’s the thing—critique is how things actually change.
When someone calls out a problem, they’re opening the door to something better. They’re saying, “Hey, let’s not settle for less than what we deserve.”
Most of us just want to be liked. We want to blend in and avoid conflict. But sometimes, the most loving thing you can do for someone—or for a community—is to tell the truth. To say, “This just isn’t good enough,” even if it feels uncomfortable in the moment.
Critique isn’t about tearing things down. It’s about building something stronger.
Think about it—the world doesn’t change just because everyone’s polite. Real change happens when people are willing to ask for more. When someone speaks up, they’re showing that they care—not just about themselves, but about everyone who comes after.
It’s easy to wave criticism away as negativity. But honestly, the people who care the most? They’re often the ones who refuse to look away. The ones who truly believe that things can get better—and are willing to put in the effort to make it happen.
